title: HKC One Year On: Why Demolition Remains Subdued
section_path: HKC One Year On: Why Demolition Remains Subdued
section_path_text: HKC One Year On: Why Demolition Remains Subdued
summary:
Main
Image reference: assets/2026-07-24_hkc-one-year-on-why-demolition-remains-subdued_img_rgb-color-brs-shipbrokers-monogram-l_c365f35f1de5.png
One year after the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships (HKC) entered into force, the widely expected wave of demolition has still not arrived. When the HKC formally took effect in June 2025, many in the market expected a visible increase in recycling volumes, supported by an ageing global fleet, tighter environmentals regulation and rising newbuilding deliveries. In theory, all these factors should have accelerated the exit of older tonnage.
